data.body: First hypothesis supported by the sweep's `icacls` step (run 44456347985, job 135332660982): a fresh `tempfile.mkdtemp()` directory on the Windows runner (Python 3.13) carries exactly `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(OI)(CI)(F)`, `BUILTIN\Administrators:(OI)(CI)(F)`, `OWNER RIGHTS:(OI)(CI)(F)`, and the OWNER RIGHTS entry is inheritable, so the key copy written into it inherits the ACE Win32-OpenSSH rejects. By contrast a key minted by `ssh-keygen` gets explicit Administrators / SYSTEM / owner-user entries. Not yet checked: the key copy's own ACL (the step does not write one), which would confirm the inheritance directly.
